text.p: Sales of state holdings have now earned Morocco over 10 billion dirhams ($1.13 billion) with a recent payment by ONA group for state minority shares in three mines, the privatisation ministry said on Wednesday.
The income, under Morocco's privatisation programme started in 1993, followed privatisation of 49 companies and hotels, the ministry said.

"On top of receipts which have gone to the public Treasury and which have financed various infrastructure investment projects, there should be added investment pledges by different purchasers which total 2.263 billion dirhams..," it added in a statement sent to Reuters.
These pledges could not "fail to have a positive impact on job creation and general economic activity," it said.

Despite this, the ministry added: "These figures, while relatively important, cannot hide the delay in the execution of the privatisation programme which envisages the cession of 113 enterprises and hotels before December 31, 1998."
It was urgent that present privatisation procedures which had become a source of inefficiency be changed, it added.

ONA group, the country's biggest private conglomerate, paid 194.9 million dirhams for the holdings in copper, cobalt and fluorite mines. It had already bought, last September, 36.07 percent of a first tranche sale in a silver mine, Societe Metallurgique d'Imiter (SMI).

"Under the terms of the transfer to ONA group of the batch formed of the four mining firms, SMI, CTT, SAMINE and SOMIFER, we envisage ceding the 33 percent of the SMI capital still held by the state," the ministry said.
"This operation, which introduces to the Casablanca bourse a top-level mining firm, should be completed before the end of the first half of 1997."

A ministry source said SMI had been transformed into a mining holding company which covered a wide range of minerals which helped to prevent it being affected by price movements of a particular mineral.
"It is a good candidate for the stock exchange because it (the spread of minerals) tends to stabilise your income flow," he said.
A draft law is now before parliament on privatising the telecommunications sector, and splitting the postal and communications services into two groups.
